texts.small-study.warning:
Primary asymmetry test: Classical Egger test
Result: evidence of small-study effects (p = < 0.001)
Usable studies: 12
Estimate: 5.872 (95% CI 5.346 to 6.398)

Funnel plot asymmetry can reflect publication bias, heterogeneity, study design, or chance.

Interpret the plots and tests together. No single result proves or rules out publication bias.

texts.small-study.tests:
Classical Egger test (primary)
  Studies: 12
  Result: Evidence of small-study effects (p = < 0.001).
  Test statistic: 24.87
  Coefficient: 5.872 (SE 0.2361; 95% CI 5.346 to 6.398)
  Model: multiplicative Egger regression

Mixed-effects Egger test (additional)
  Studies: 12
  Result: Evidence of small-study effects (p = < 0.001).
  Test statistic: 3.595
  Coefficient: 5.872 (SE 1.633; 95% CI 2.670 to 9.073)
  Model: REML mixed-effects meta-regression

Begg-Mazumdar test (additional)
  Studies: 12
  Result: Evidence of small-study effects (p = < 0.001).
  Test statistic: 4.526
  Coefficient: 66.00 (SE 14.58; 95% CI Not available to Not available)
  Model: Begg-Mazumdar rank correlation

texts.small-study.references:
1. Egger regression test: Egger, M., Davey Smith, G., Schneider, M., & Minder, C. (1997). Bias in meta-analysis detected by a simple, graphical test. BMJ, 315(7109), 629-634. doi:10.1136/bmj.315.7109.629.
2. Mixed-effects regression test: Sterne, J. A. C., & Egger, M. (2005). Regression methods to detect publication and other bias in meta-analysis. In Publication Bias in Meta-Analysis: Prevention, Assessment and Adjustments (pp. 99-110). Wiley.
3. Begg-Mazumdar rank test: Begg, C. B., & Mazumdar, M. (1994). Operating characteristics of a rank correlation test for publication bias. Biometrics, 50(4), 1088-1101. doi:10.2307/2533446.
4. Funnel plot axis choice: Sterne, J. A. C., & Egger, M. (2001). Funnel plots for detecting bias in meta-analysis: Guidelines on choice of axis. Journal of Clinical Epidemiology, 54(10), 1046-1055. doi:10.1016/S0895-4356(01)00377-8.
5. Contour-enhanced funnel plots: Peters, J. L., Sutton, A. J., Jones, D. R., Abrams, K. R., & Rushton, L. (2008). Contour-enhanced meta-analysis funnel plots help distinguish publication bias from other causes of asymmetry. Journal of Clinical Epidemiology, 61(10), 991-996. doi:10.1016/j.jclinepi.2007.11.010.
6. Trim-and-fill method: Duval, S., & Tweedie, R. (2000). Trim and fill: A simple funnel-plot-based method of testing and adjusting for publication bias in meta-analysis. Biometrics, 56(2), 455-463. doi:10.1111/j.0006-341X.2000.00455.x.
7. Implementation reference: Viechtbauer, W. (2010). Conducting meta-analyses in R with the metafor package. Journal of Statistical Software, 36(3), 1-48. doi:10.18637/jss.v036.i03.
texts.small-study.method-details:
Classical Egger test
  Package: meta 8.5-0
  Predictor: SE
  Weighting: inverse variance
  Inference: t-based meta::metabias test
  Degrees of freedom: 10.00
  Exact p-value: 0.00000000025241389
  Call: meta::metabias(x=prepared.meta.model, method.bias='Egger', k.min=10, level=0.95)

Mixed-effects Egger test
  Package: metafor 5.0-1
  Predictor: SE
  Weighting: inverse-variance weights with REML heterogeneity
  Inference: z test from metafor::regtest
  Degrees of freedom: Not available
  Exact p-value: 0.00032469669
  Call: metafor::regtest(x=prepared.effects, sei=prepared.standard.errors, model='rma', predictor='sei', ret.fit=TRUE, level=95)

Begg-Mazumdar test
  Package: meta 8.5-0
  Predictor: rank correlation of standardized effects and variance
  Weighting: not applicable (Kendall rank-based test)
  Inference: z test from Kendall rank correlation
  Degrees of freedom: Not available
  Exact p-value: 0.0000060170826
  Call: meta::metabias(x=prepared.meta.model, method.bias='Begg', k.min=10, level=0.95)
